sections.title: Market review
sections.body:
## The week's tape: quiet index, loud dispersion
The completed week through the 2026-09-04 close was flat at the index — SPY +0.1% on the week (ow_rotation, asOf 2026-09-04) — but the calm hid wide sector dispersion. Semiconductors and ag inputs led; consumer discretionary, cybersecurity and SaaS lagged. Cross-asset conditions stayed benign into the snapshot: HY OAS 2.65 (asOf 2026-09-03), VIX 14.52, 10y 4.788%, 2s10s 41.3. Treat the low-vol, tight-credit backdrop as an observation, not proof of complacency or of what is priced.

## Hardware over software, inside the same tech tape
The sharpest weekly signal was intra-tech dispersion. On the 2026-09-04 basket window, Memory/Storage led at +7.6% (+7.5% vs SPY, 4 of 4 members), Foundry +5.4% (+5.3%, 4 of 4) and Computer/GPU +3.4% (+3.3%, 6 of 6). Against that, Software/SaaS printed -4.7% (-4.8% vs SPY, 6 of 6) and Cybersecurity -6.9% (-7.0%, 4 of 4). The sector ETF read is milder — XLK +0.9% (+0.7% excess) — because XLK blends the software drag; the single-name baskets isolate the hardware bid. The plausible mechanism is an AI-capex/hardware rotation with memory and foundry as the tightest-supply links, but the ETF-vs-basket gap is a reminder that relative outperformance alel is not a clean cause, and 4-member baskets carry high single-name beta: one name can carry a +7.5% print. The next observable is whether the hardware lead survives ADBE's 2026-09-10 report and holds on a fresh SPY bar past 2026-09-04.

## Ag inputs: the week's outright leader
The el-nino-ag-2026 basket (DBA, MOS, NTR, DE, equal-weight) was the top rotation row: +6.6% on the week, +6.5% excess over SPY, and it extends over longer windows (+12.9% 4w, +15.7% 12w; +13.3% and +11.6% excess). That is real medium-term leadership, not a one-week pop. The competing explanation is commodity beta rather than the El Niño thesis specifically — the basket mixes a soft/grain ETF with fertilizer and equipment names that trade on separate drivers, and no dated grain print is in this evidence to attribute the move. The kill condition (ONI back below +0.5 two months running, or -10% vs SPY over 60 sessions) is not met.

## Rates, policy and the oil undertone
The front and long end barely moved into the snapshot: 2y 4.375%, 10y 4.788%, both effectively unchanged. The live policy read has the 9/16 FOMC at a 57.9% HIKE probability (asOf 2026-09-07) — a genuine hike bias, not a cut, which frames the rate-sensitive laggards (XLRE -1.2%, XLY -2.0% on the week). Since the close, an oil-supply story has run through the tape: Unusual Whales carried "OIL RISES AS REPORTS OF A STRIKE ON SAUDI ARAMCO'S JAZAN REFINERY... WTI AT $92.43" (2026-09-08T00:23:19Z) and Goldman raising Brent/WTI forecasts by $5 (2026-09-08T00:24:05Z). Commodities in the frame show WTI 92.24 (+0.83%) and gold 4421.55 (-0.19%) as of 2026-09-08T00:39:48.781Z. These are post-close snapshots and headlines, not weekly changes; XLE has no current bar (newest 2026-07-13), so the energy read is untested here.

Coverage note: this week's `close` reports carried no dated edit prose, so the review is anchored on the 2026-09-04 basket/rotation window plus timestamped headlines; I have not reconstructed intra-week paths that the evidence does not support.

sections.title: Outlook
sections.body:
## Can the hardware lead hold
The question for next week is whether Memory/Storage, Foundry and GPU leadership survives contact with a live SaaS catalyst. ADBE reports post-close 2026-09-10, inside the coming seven days, with a 6.9% implied move (dte 7) and IV rank 68.84 — the one dated single-name event that can either deepen the software drag or begin to close the hardware-vs-software gap. Confirmation of the hardware read is another up week in the semi baskets on a fresh SPY bar; invalidation is a broad tech rally led by SaaS after ADBE, which would reframe this week's dispersion as noise around thin baskets. Reverse risk: the semi baskets are 4-6 names, so one reversal can erase a basket's excess.

## Ag leadership vs commodity beta
The ag basket's multi-window lead is the most durable relative trend in the evidence. It persists if the grain/soft complex stays bid; it fades toward its kill line if the instruments give back 10% vs SPY over the 60-session window or the ONI trigger reverses. Watch whether DE (equipment) and MOS/NTR (fertilizer) keep moving together or diverge — divergence would argue commodity beta over a single El Niño driver.

## Rates and oil as the macro overhang
With the 9/16 FOMC carrying a 57.9% hike probability (later context, not this week), the near-term risk is that the oil-supply headlines harden into a realized inflation impulse before that meeting. WTI at 92.24 and the Goldman forecast bump are the tell to track; a sustained crude push with a firmer dollar would pressure the rate-sensitive laggards further and could lift energy, which is untested here for lack of a current XLE bar. The confirming observable is HY OAS and VIX: both benign into the close (2.65, 14.52), so any widening or a VIX break above the mid-teens would be the first sign the quiet index tape is ending. No FOMC decision, no CPI print and no policy meeting falls inside the coming seven days in the supplied calendar; ADBE is the singular dated catalyst.
